title: Google's Excellent Wireless Charging Puck and Stand Is 50 Percent Off Right Now
gist: Google's Pixelsnap Qi2 25W charger with stand is discounted 50 percent to $35, below the $40 price of the bare puck, which the writer attributes to a likely accessory refresh alongside the imminent Pixel 11 range. The underlying signal is Qi2 25W convergence: one Google-branded magnetic charger now delivers full 25W to Pixel 10 Pro XL, Samsung Galaxy S26 Ultra, and iPhone 17 alike.

insights.claim: Google's Pixelsnap charger delivers up to 25 watts to Pixel 10 Pro XL, Samsung Galaxy S26 Ultra, and the iPhone 17 series, and 15 watts to older iPhones, the rest of the Pixel 10 range, and various Samsung phones.
insights.speaker: Simon Hill
insights.so_what: A single accessory now serves all three major phone ecosystems at full speed, collapsing the accessory market's platform segmentation and commoditizing first-party chargers.
insights.locator: The Pixelsnap sports the very latest Qi2 25W release

insights.claim: Qi2 wireless charging works like Apple's MagSafe, using a ring of magnets to ensure perfect alignment for the most efficient and speedy wireless charging possible.
insights.speaker: Simon Hill
insights.so_what: The industry has effectively adopted Apple's magnetic-alignment approach as an open standard, eroding MagSafe's accessory moat.
insights.locator: If you’re not familiar, Qi2 wireless charging

insights.claim: The Pixelsnap charger and stand bundle is discounted from $70 to $35, which is less than the $40 that the charger puck alone normally costs.
insights.speaker: Simon Hill
insights.so_what: A bundle priced below its own component signals inventory clearance rather than a promotional discount.

insights.claim: With the Pixel 11 range just around the corner, Google may be prepping a new charger, though the existing Pixelsnap is likely to work with the new phones.
insights.speaker: Simon Hill
insights.so_what: Deep first-party accessory discounts are a reliable leading indicator of an imminent flagship launch cycle.
insights.locator: With the Pixel 11 range just around the corner

insights.claim: The Pixelsnap ships without a power adapter, requiring a separate purchase such as the $16 Anker Nano 30W.
insights.speaker: Simon Hill
insights.so_what: Unbundled power bricks keep headline accessory prices low while pushing attach revenue to third parties like Anker.
insights.locator: The only thing missing is the power adapter

insights.claim: The Pixelsnap puck detaches from its stand and sticks to the back of the phone, letting the user keep scrolling while charging, a design that treats charging as portable rather than stationary.
insights.speaker: Simon Hill
insights.so_what: Magnetic detachable pucks blur the line between wireless chargers and battery packs, a category convergence accessory makers are pricing into new designs.
insights.locator: Speed might not be the most important thing

insights.claim: Charging speed matters little for overnight users, so the stand's real value is the nightstand and alarm-clock use case rather than throughput.
insights.speaker: Simon Hill
insights.so_what: If wattage is not the buying criterion for most users, the wireless-charging spec race has limited pricing power and differentiation moves to form factor.
insights.locator: Perfect if you want to prop your phone up
